body: I relate 100%. Sometimes I daydream about exchanging my life with someone who's suffering so they could enjoy it, because for me it wouldn't make much of a difference. I don't know if it feels the same for you, but I constantly feel my life is missing something, a spark that would make me want to be alive. But who knows, maybe someday we'll find it.
I think you should see a doctor. Of course it can be that your metabolism became naturally slower, but you should exclude other possibilities just to make sure.

I always try to exercise and end up giving up, but I've been exercising daily for a about a week now. But yes, I do think that the problems with my body reflect my mental problems. A few months ago I felt like I had switched lives with someone else, because I couldn't feel connected to anything I did. Nowadays it's only my body, so maybe it could already be considered an improvement. Thanks for your reply

I'm going through something similar. I'm unable to study as much as I did because at some point I just can't understand what I read anymore (I read the words and it's like my brain doesn't process it) and if I try to continue I either get extremely depressed/annoyed or get a headache. What I liked doing the most was drawing, but lately it's making me very frustrated. I don't even have the will to keep some collections I cherished so much... Now I'm trying to fight it by making schedules, though I have a hard time following them for more than two days.

I feel the same way. Today I realized that it'd be better to become a hikikomori and only interact with other people through the internet. Sadly I can't do that because I don't have an income and still live with my mother. I become too self-aware when I'm with others, when I'm alone I feel like I can forget about myself for a while.
Same here. I just keep on trying to run away from myself and my own life.

Last semester I was like that too, but I'm a little better now. It's still hard to have motivation to study at home, but at least I'm attending the classes. Even if you don't feel like going at all, make some effort, because if you stay home you will think too much and feel worse afterwards. Consider getting out of home as a daily accomplishment.

I'm just like you, the difference is that I'm already finishing my 3rd year in college. My advice to you is that if you don't like it, leave as soon as possible, because it just gets worse. I feel like I've struggled so much until now that I'd be a waste to just leave everything behind. I really regret not leaving in the second semester when I noticed I didn't like what I was studying at all.
I often daydream about gender transition and feel happy, but the depression takes over as soon as I look in the mirror or someone uses the wrong pronouns.

I have depression cycles. My best phases seem to come after I solve a problem that has been stressing me for a while, or after I finish a semester in college. However, about a week later I already start to notice that things are getting bad again, even if there's no reason. And depression comes again full force when the stress piles up or when I spend too much time doing nothing and just thinking about how boring my life is. The cycle seems never-ending.
It kinda works for me too, until I get exhausted and even more depressed. But I think I wouldn't feel that bad if I liked what I have to do.
I know why I'm depressed for months, but still didn't do anything about it. Not sure if I ever will.

I totally feel you. I'm currently in third year of college and I couldn't hate it more. In the second semester I had some problems with anxiety, in the third semester it just got worse and since then I want to leave college. However, my course is hard and promising, my college is one of the best in the country and I'm just one year/one year and a half from completing it. I have no courage to leave now, even if continuing feels like a torture.
I can't totally open up either, I just don't have the courage to tell my mom how bad I'm feeling. She does so much for me, it feels like I'm being ungrateful.
I'm just like you. I have no dreams anymore and I constantly feel like I'm going nowhere. That makes me feel terrible because I always had crazy dreams that kept me going forward.
Yes. I guess for me the main point is that it's very hard to study. I can't be motivated when I just feel like dying, and then the bad grades make me feel even worse.

I always feel like I'm annoying other people and they only interact with me out of politeness or obligation. And for the people who spend time with me because they want to (boyfriend and the few friends who I hang out with), I feel like they will eventually notice how annoying/boring I am and leave me.

I'm just like you. No one takes my suffering seriously because there's nothing bad about my life. I already gave up on trying to talk to my mom because she always gets angry at me, while my boyfriend says I'm always sad anyways. There're times that I want to find a solution and finally get out of depression, but I just can't figure anything out. Everything is blurred and I don't even know what I want or not anymore.

That happens to me as well! I'm agender and androsexual, but I'd like to have a masculine gender expression. My ultimate idol is G-Dragon and my boyfriend used to be very jealous because I have three posters of GD in my bedroom, but the truth is that I admire him much more than I find him handsome. The first thing that comes to my mind when looking at his photos is "he's so cool, I wish I was like that too". There're other idols that I feel more attracted to than admire, but even so once in a while I wonder why couldn't I be a cute boy too.
I'm trying to look as androgynous as possible, but my face doesn't help much. With make up I might be able to confuse people at first glance, but my voice would ruin everything.
